oracleRisk.summary: Aster manages USDF backing through custodial USDT and offchain delta-neutral positions, without publishing a user-CDP liquidation oracle or market-specific feed inventory.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research
branchApplicability.rationale: USDF mints and redeems against USDT while Aster manages backing and hedge positions through Ceffu and Binance. Holders do not open permissionless collateralized debt positions with onchain per-collateral liquidation thresholds, auctions, backstops, or shutdown branches, so the V9 CDP branch inventory does not apply.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDF is natively issued on BSC through the USDFEarn deposit-and-cap path, while the same token contract carries LayerZero V2 direct OFT burn/mint machinery. The BSC owner Timelock and EndpointV2 delegate Safe can configure the transfer rail, but current peers and transfer-limit configurations are zero for the checked mainnet EIDs and no BSC-mainnet remote USDF deployment is identified. Bridge coverage is therefore verified but dormant and unresolved, not an active favorable external-validation route.

routes.protocol: LayerZero V2 direct OFT (dormant remote route surface)
routes.reviewNote: The BSC deployment is the verified canonical native-issuance token and also inherits LayerZero V2 OFT burn/mint machinery. At BSC block 116356251 on 2026-08-16, peers(eid) for Ethereum (30101), Arbitrum (30110), Optimism (30111), Base (30184), and Polygon (30109) all returned bytes32(0), and the corresponding transferLimitConfigs reads were zero. Aster's registry and checked deployment repository identify no BSC-mainnet remote USDF deployment, so the remote representation route remains unresolved/dormant and no active external-validation tier is asserted. Any future route is supply-conserving only when source debit/burn and authenticated destination credit/mint are paired.

controls.label: USDF BSC direct OFT burn/mint route

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: At BSC block 116356251, peers(eid) for Ethereum (30101), Arbitrum (30110), Optimism (30111), Base (30184), and Polygon (30109) all returned bytes32(0). The official LayerZero reference requires a paired deployment and directional setPeer configuration; no active remote USDF destination is proven.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The corresponding transferLimitConfigs(eid) reads were zero for every checked mainnet destination; no active route-specific limiter was identified.
routeChecks.caps: The direct OFT route is supply-conserving only when source _debit burns/debits and authenticated destination _credit mints/credits. The token's co-located native USDFEarn mint path remains separately bounded by deposit receipt and USDFMaxSupply.

controls.capDescription: No active route-specific transfer limit or remote destination is currently proven; future bridge issuance depends on paired source debit and authenticated destination credit rather than independent native issuance.
controls.evidence: At BSC block 116356251, the verified USDF token source inherited LayerZero OFT send/receive semantics: _debit applies the custom destination limiter before the OFT burn path, while authenticated _credit is the corresponding destination mint path. All checked mainnet peers and transfer-limit configurations were zero, so this bridge machinery is dormant and no remote representation is asserted. Its burn/mint capability remains scoreable under Bridge Risk without inflating native Mint Authority.

controls.label: USDF BSC direct OFT owner Timelock

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: USDF.owner() returned Timelock 0xe829a87f4dfa41b032d8b6feca6c2213d6ee1861 at BSC block 116356251. The owner can call setPeer and activate or replace a remote LayerZero route; checked mainnet peers were all zero at the observation block.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The 21,600-second Timelock is also the native USDF DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and USDFEarn UUPS upgrade authority, which remain separately authored in Mint Authority. This Bridge Risk control covers only its direct OFT peer-configuration capability.

controls.evidence: At BSC block 116356251, USDF.owner() returned the 6-hour Timelock 0xe829a87f4dfa41b032d8b6feca6c2213d6ee1861. Its owner-controlled setPeer surface can configure the direct OFT's future remote route, but no checked mainnet peer was set. Native token-admin, cap, role, and mint-logic powers of this same Timelock remain in Mint Authority and are not double-counted here.

controls.label: USDF BSC LayerZero Endpoint delegate Safe

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: EndpointV2.delegates(USDF) returned Safe 0xa8c0c6ee62f5ad95730fe23ccf37d1c1ffaa1c3f at BSC block 116356251. This endpoint delegate controls LayerZero messaging configuration, while the USDF token's checked peers remained zero and no remote destination contract was identified.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Safe's EndpointV2 delegate relationship is bridge messaging administration. Its separate USDFEarn ADMIN_ROLE cap authority and delayed native governance powers remain in Mint Authority; no bridge destination token administrator was identified.

controls.evidence: At BSC block 116356251, EndpointV2.delegates(USDF) returned Safe 0xa8c0c6ee62f5ad95730fe23ccf37d1c1ffaa1c3f. Current Safe reads returned threshold 4 with 7 owners, no enabled modules, zero guard/module-guard storage, and the standard Safe Compatibility Fallback Handler. This Safe is therefore a verified EndpointV2 messaging administrator for the dormant direct OFT surface, while its native cap and governance controls remain separately authored in Mint Authority.
